findings.title: Unsubscribe is a state-changing GET that also returns the full topic page
findings.body: The new unsubscribe action is reached only via GET routes (config/routes.rb lines 440-441), yet it both mutates user state (`tu.save!` at line 113) and returns the rendered topic view (`perform_show_response` at line 115). GET requests must be idempotent. The unsubscribe URL is embedded in every notification email (app/mailers/user_notifications.rb line 295, config/locales/server.en.yml), and link-previewers, antivirus scanners, corporate proxies, and prefetching mail clients routinely fetch URLs found in emails. Each prefetch will silently toggle the user's notification level between regular and muted. There is no CSRF token (and none can be on a GET), so there is also no defence against any cross-site request that triggers navigation to the URL. The expected UX for an unsubscribe click is a short confirmation / re-subscribe page, not the entire topic with all posts; as shipped, the response is the wrong page and the action is unsafe to expose as a GET.

findings.title: Unsubscribe action has no authorization check on the topic
findings.body: After `@topic_view = TopicView.new(...)` the action immediately looks up the user's TopicUser row (line 105), mutates it (line 108-111) and saves it (line 113) without ever calling `guardian.ensure_can_see!(@topic_view.topic)` (compare with `mute`, `re_pin`, `clear_pin`, etc. in the same controller which all do call `ensure_can_see!`). Any logged-in user who knows or guesses a topic id can visit `/t/<slug>/<id>/unsubscribe` and silently unsubscribe from any topic, including topics in read-restricted categories or topics they have been removed from. Because the action then calls `perform_show_response`, the rendered response can also expose topic content the user is not authorised to see when `TopicView.new` does not raise (e.g. a topic in a category the user still has limited access to).

findings.title: NoMethodError when the user has no TopicUser row for the topic
findings.body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` (line 105) returns nil for any user who has never opened the topic but is still on the recipient list of the notification email (the common case for someone clicking 'unsubscribe' from an email). The very next line, `if tu.notification_level > ...` (line 107), then calls `notification_level` on nil and raises `NoMethodError`, producing a 500 for what is the primary intended use of the link. The action should either use `TopicUser.get`/`TopicUser.change` (which upserts) or guard explicitly against a nil `tu` (and decide what muting means for a user who never had a row).

findings.title: Server renders topics/show instead of the unsubscribe confirmation page
findings.body: After saving the new notification level, `perform_show_response` (line 115) renders `topics/show`, i.e. the full topic view including all posts, breadcrumbs, reply controls, etc. The PR also adds a complete client-side unsubscribe experience (`controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, `routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`, `views/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, the new `.topic-unsubscribe` SCSS block, and the `topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications` / `change_notification_state` i18n strings), but the server pre-empts all of it by rendering the show template. The new Ember route, controller, view, template, styles, and locale strings are unreachable through the URL the email links to. The action should either render an unsubscribe-specific server template (`render :unsubscribe`) or redirect (e.g. 302 to `topic.relative_url`) so the user lands on a confirmation / change-notification-state page rather than the topic itself.

findings.title: No assertion that the per-topic unsubscribe URL reaches the email body
findings.body: The new spec only adds `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"` to the `MessageBuilder` constructor (line 172) and the server locale now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}` into `unsubscribe_link` (config/locales/server.en.yml), but neither of the two existing assertions in this context checks that the per-topic URL ends up in the rendered email. The current tests only assert the `user_preferences_url` is in the body and that the `List-Unsubscribe` header is present — both of which were true before this PR. A test such as `expect(message_with_unsubscribe.body).to include('/t/1234/unsubscribe')` (and an equivalent against `html_part`) is required to lock in the new behaviour; without it a regression in `message_builder.rb` or the locale string will go undetected. There are also no controller specs covering the new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action (authorization, slug redirect, nil `tu`, notification-level toggle).

findings.title: Typo in computed property: stopNotificiationsText
findings.body: The computed property is named `stopNotificiationsText` (N-o-t-i-f-i-c-a-t-i-o-n-s, three i's) and the same misspelling is used in `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs` line 3. The double mistake cancels out so the template currently renders, but the property name is wrong and grep / future edits will trip over it. It should be `stopNotificationsText`. (Note this only matters once the server-side bug above is fixed and the unsubscribe template is actually reached.)
